commands.name: file-organizer
commands.description: Organize files into category folders by extension
help: Organizes root-level files in a directory into categorized subfolders
based on file extension (Images, Videos, Documents, Audio, etc.).
-Path <path>   Directory to organize. Default: current directory.
-WhatIf        Preview what would move without making any changes.
Handles filename collisions by appending _2, _3, ... instead of overwriting.

commands.name: file-organizer-ai
help: Classifies files using keyword rules first, then extension map,
with optional Ollama AI as a final fallback for unmatched files.
-Source <path>   Directory to organize. Default: current directory.
-UseAI           Enable Ollama AI fallback (requires Ollama installed).
-Model <model>   Ollama model name. Default: gemma:2b.
-DryRun          Preview without moving files.
Outputs organizer.log and organizer-metadata.json to the destination folder.

commands.name: disk-cleaner
commands.description: Analyze disk usage, find duplicates and large files
help: Interactive TUI for analyzing disk usage. Groups files by type,
finds duplicates (SHA256), and surfaces large files.
-Path <path>   Directory to scan. Default: current directory.
Deletions go to the Recycle Bin -- nothing is permanently removed.

commands.name: app-uninstaller
commands.description: List installed apps and uninstall interactively
help: Keyboard-driven TUI listing all installed Win32/MSI apps with size,
install date, publisher, and last-used time.
-IncludeStore   Also show Microsoft Store (AppX) packages.
Keys:
Up / Down        Move cursor
Left / Right     Page through list
Space            Toggle selection
Ctrl+U           Uninstall selected (requires typing YES to confirm)
F / C            Open / clear name+publisher filter
S                Cycle sort: Name / Size / Date / Publisher / Usage
Ctrl+R           Rescan installed apps
Requires Administrator elevation (auto-prompted on launch).

commands.name: env
commands.description: Manage environment variables, PATH, .env files, and profiles
help: Manage Windows environment variables (User and System scopes).
env --list [--user | --system] [--json]    list all variables
env --get <NAME>                           show a variable
env --set NAME=VALUE [--system]            set a variable (default: User scope)
env --delete <NAME> [--system]             delete a variable
env --temp NAME=VALUE                      set a session-only variable
env --path --list [--user|--system]        show PATH entries with validation (default: user)
env --path --get <term> [--user|--system]  search PATH entries by name
env --path --add "C:\A" "C:\B" [--system]   add one or more directories to PATH
env --path --remove "C:\A" "C:\B" [--system] remove one or more directories from PATH
env --load <file.env>                      load KEY=VALUE pairs from a .env file
env --export <file.env>                    export User variables to a .env file
env --profile                              list available profiles
env --profile <name>                       apply all variables from a named profile
env --generate node | python | dotnet      generate a starter .env template
Profiles are JSON files stored in <install-dir>\env-profiles\<name>.json.
Sensitive values (KEY, SECRET, TOKEN, PASSWORD) are masked in list output.

commands.name: search
help: Search filenames or file contents recursively.
pt search <query>                  search filenames (supports wildcards: *.json)
pt search <query> --content        search inside files, show matching lines
Smart filters (restrict file types):
--logs   .log, .txt
--json   .json
--code   .js, .ts, .cs, .ps1
--path <dir>         root directory to search (default: current directory)
--limit <n>          cap number of results (default: 50)
--open <n>           open result number n with default app
--excl <list>        comma-separated dirs or filenames to exclude (e.g. node_modules,dist)
--jsonout            output results as JSON
Results sorted by last modified (filename mode) or match count (content mode).

commands.name: run
commands.description: Execute predefined workflow scripts from run.config.json
help: Execute named workflows defined in run.config.json (current dir) or pt.config.json (install dir).
pt run <workflow>               run a workflow
pt run <workflow> --dry          preview steps without executing
pt run <workflow> --continue     keep running even if a step fails
pt run <workflow> --env <name>   apply an env profile before running
pt run --list                    list all available workflows
pt run --list --jsonout          list workflows as JSON
Config file (run.config.json) format:
"scripts": {
"dev": [
"npm install",
"npm run dev"
"build": [
{ "cmd": "npm ci", "if": "node_modules missing" },
{ "parallel": ["npm run frontend", "npm run backend"] },
{ "cmd": "dotnet build", "timeout": 120 }
Step formats:
"cmd"            simple string command
{ cmd, if, timeout }  conditional / timed command
{ parallel: [...] }   run commands concurrently
Condition expressions (used in the 'if' field):
node_modules missing       true when node_modules dir is absent
dir missing: <path>        true when directory is absent
file missing: <path>       true when file is absent
env: <VAR>                 true when env variable is set
env missing: <VAR>         true when env variable is not set
Config priority: run.config.json (current dir) > pt.config.json (install dir).

commands.name: json
commands.description: Format, minify, validate, query, and patch JSON files
help: JSON utility -- inspect and modify JSON from files or stdin.
pt json format   <file.json>                     pretty-print JSON
pt json minify   <file.json>                     compact single-line JSON
pt json validate <file.json>                     check syntax (shows error + position)
pt json query    <file.json> <key.path>          extract a value by dot path
pt json set      <file.json> <key.path> <value>  update a value and save in place
Pipe support -- stdin replaces the file argument:
cat file.json | pt json format
cat file.json | pt json query user.address.city
cat file.json | pt json set user.name John > out.json
Dot-path examples:
user.name           string or object property
items.0.title       first element of an array
config.flags.2      third element of a nested array
Value coercion for 'set':
true / false        stored as boolean
null                stored as JSON null
42 / 3.14           stored as number
anything else       stored as string

commands.name: port
commands.description: Inspect, kill, list, watch, and find free ports
help: TCP port inspector and process manager.
pt port --get <port>             Show all connections on a port
pt port --get --pid <id>         Show connections by PID
pt port --get --name <name>      Show connections by process name
pt port --kill <port>            Kill process using a port (confirms first)
pt port --kill <port> --force    Skip confirmation
pt port --fix <port>             Detect and prompt to kill (same as --kill)
pt port --list                   List all active TCP connections
pt port --list --range <n>       Limit to first N results
pt port --list --s <n> --e <n>   Filter by port number range
pt port --watch <port>           Watch port state in real-time (Ctrl+C exits)
pt port --free                   Find first free port (default range 1024-65535)
pt port --free --s <n> --e <n>   Find free port in custom range
pt port --json                   Output as JSON (combine with any command)
Color coding: Green=LISTEN, Red=ESTABLISHED, Yellow=TIME_WAIT/CLOSE_WAIT
